description: Shared ticket 07/21 capture matrix. Paths describe shell and transport mechanics, the exact startup rewrite, and the fidelity each mechanism produces. Cells enumerate the Host/Arch/Shell matrix with the capture tier, release classification, and evidence kind: observed (a real run recorded here), ci (a required job in .github/workflows/release.yml, not run on this machine), or manual (a runnable procedure a human performs). observedRuns record only what actually ran here: macOS arm64 and macOS amd64 under Rosetta 2, Linux Docker arm64/amd64, and the Linux SSH lab used to validate the remote harness. Windows and FreeBSD cells never claim an observation. Erroring in this file is a test failure, not product behavior.
fidelityLegend: Path fidelity: tier is the capture tier; exact means a real shell was observed reporting that field, observed means a real shell reported the field but not the value, missing means the mechanism cannot observe it, and manual/planned means this machine did not run it. A path's verification covers only the platforms named in observedPlatforms; every platform has its own cell truth. Cell evidence: observed cells cite only a real recorded run (observed.fidelity is an observation claim); ci cells cite a required release-workflow job and never claim a local run; manual cells record runnable steps for an unrun environment and are never observations. Tier 1 is the authoritative session hook, Tier 2 native OSC 133/7 without a Netcatty hook, and Tier 3 typed input plus prompt detection.

cells.name: windows-amd64-nushell

manual.runner: GitHub Actions windows-2025 (x86_64) or windows-11-arm (arm64); not run on this machine
steps: In PowerShell: winget install --id Nushell.Nushell --exact --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements --silent; then open a new PowerShell: $nu = (Get-Command nu.exe).Source; if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $nu)) { throw 'nu.exe is missing' }; & $nu --version

In that PowerShell, prove this nushell build honors XDG_CONFIG_HOME (absolute path; nushell/nushell#12118): $env:XDG_CONFIG_HOME = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'netcatty-nu-xdg'; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force (Join-Path $env:XDG_CONFIG_HOME 'nushell') | Out-Null; 'print "xdg-ok"' | Set-Content (Join-Path $env:XDG_CONFIG_HOME 'nushell\config.nu'); & $nu -c '$nu.default-config-dir'; Remove-Item Env:XDG_CONFIG_HOME -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Remove-Item -Recurse -Force (Join-Path $env:TEMP 'netcatty-nu-xdg'). Require the printed directory to end with netcatty-nu-xdg\nushell. If it prints %APPDATA%\nushell, this build ignores XDG_CONFIG_HOME and the test cannot read its isolated config; record the run as unverified, not PASS.
In that PowerShell: $env:NETCATTY_TEST_NU = $nu; go test ./adapters/shellhook -run '^TestRealNushellWithoutHookKeepsNativeCapture$' -count=1 -v

Require PASS with Tier 2, the native cwd, no Netcatty exit code, and the test's user-config marker; the test writes config.nu under its own XDG_CONFIG_HOME. The Windows planner does not install a nushell hook. If the preflight printed %APPDATA%\nushell, a PASS is impossible and the cell stays unverified.

cells.evidence: Not observed here and not run on any Windows machine. The procedure starts with an XDG_CONFIG_HOME preflight because the test writes its isolated config under XDG_CONFIG_HOME/nushell and, since nushell/nushell#12118, an absolute XDG_CONFIG_HOME is honored on Windows too; a build that resolves %APPDATA%\nushell instead fails the test's user-config assertion, which is a failure, not a PASS. Tier 2 only, non-blocking. Windows PowerShell fidelity comes from the CI gate jobs, not this cell.

cells.name: windows-amd64-zsh

manual.runner: GitHub Actions windows-2025 (x86_64) or windows-11-arm (arm64); not run on this machine
steps: Install the shell: bash ships with Git for Windows; install zsh and fish from MSYS2 (winget install MSYS2.MSYS2, then in the MSYS2 shell pacman -S --needed zsh fish). Record each --version.
Put the shell, or the MSYS2 usr/bin directory, on PATH. For fish, set $env:NETCATTY_TEST_FISH = (Get-Command fish.exe).Source in PowerShell.
In Netcatty open Settings > Logs and confirm History capture hook is off. The Windows planner only installs the hook for PowerShell, so zsh runs unhooked either way.
Open a local session that starts zsh with its login flag: zsh -l.
